newsitem.title: SPAIN: Disney in talks to build theme park in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Disney in talks to build theme park in Spain.

text.p: Walt Disney Co is among several U.S. entertainment groups negotiating to build a new theme park on the eastern coast of Spain, a local official said on Friday.
The regional government of Valencia is in talks with Disney, Paramount and Universal Studios over plans to build a large theme park near the sun and sea resort of Alicante.

"The regional president Eduardo Zaplano went to the U.S. with a delegation last week and met company heads, including at Disney, to discuss the construction of a theme park in the south of the region," a local government spokeswoman told Reuters.
The exact location of the theme park had not been decided but it will be located in the province of Alicante, near the popular Costa Blanca tourist resort of the same name.

"We still don't know what type of park it would be and negotiations now centre on whether it would be better to build it together with one of the large groups or give it its own name, like Port Aventura," the official said.

The Spanish delegation met Disney officials in Orlando, Florida, last Thursday including the multinational's Spanish partner. They also met former Disney vice-chairman Steven Backer, now a theme park consultant.
Zaplana visited Disney and Universal theme parks in Orlando before heading to New York on Friday for talks with officials at Universal and Merrill Lynch.

Disney's first European venture, its Euro Disney complex near Paris, had a rocky start and is still shaky although it is expected to make a profit for the second year in a row. Rainy weather and a strong French franc have helped dampen sales.
Port Aventura, a $500 million theme park south of Barcelona which opened last year, has beaten forecasts by attracting thousands of visitors lured by warm southern temperatures and nearby beaches.

The Tussauds Group, part of international media group Pearson, owns 40 percent of Port Aventura. Savings bank La Caixa owns 33.2 percent, Anheuser-Busch 20 percent and electricity group Fecsa owns 6.8 percent.
Zaplana said he hoped the Valencia theme park would significantly boost tourist revenue in the region.

"This is going to be one of the most important initiatives of this government to return its role and name to the Valencia region and revive its influence so it recuperates the prestige it lost in recent years," he said in a statement.
The regional government has offered to help finance the project to make sure it is completed as soon as possible.
